Explain to a new employee how to set up two-factor authentication (2FA) on their work account with an authenticator app, and what to do if they lose their phone.

responses.text:
1. Install an authenticator app (e.g. Microsoft or Google Authenticator) on your phone.
2. Sign in to your work account, open Security settings and choose 'Set up 2FA'.
3. Scan the QR code with the app and enter the 6-digit code to confirm.
4. Save the backup codes somewhere safe, not on the same phone.
If you lose your phone, contact IT immediately so they can revoke the old device, then sign in with a backup code and set up 2FA on your new phone.
Install an authenticator app, go to your account's security settings, scan the QR code and enter the code it shows. That's it, you're protected.
2FA adds security to your account. You should enable it. Ask IT if you have questions.

Two-factor authentication (2FA) is a crucial, comprehensive security best practice. To set up 2FA, simply enable 2FA in your settings, and 2FA will protect you. If you lose your phone, don't worry: just disable 2FA from any computer using your password, since 2FA is only an extra layer. Security is everyone's responsibility, and 2FA, multi-factor authentication and strong passwords are comprehensive best practices for comprehensive security.
